findings.finding: The exclusion rule is a deny-list over config.Config, which holds the live App PEM resolved whatever the file's key source (stage3.go:393-409); a blocklist leaves every future field on an unauthenticated route until someone classifies it.
findings.answer: SettingsOf is an allowlist; TestSettingsOfClassifiesEveryConfigField walks reflect over Config and every nested config type and fails on a field neither emitted nor in an explicit excluded map with a reason. The secret-absence predicate is named: PEM header regex, postgres://, each planted value (plan T1).

findings.finding: Required or optional on the wire is unstated; required drags a mandatory DaemonAPIVersion bump (version.go:15-17; precedents 16, 23, 28) and eight fixture/literal sites, and makes daemon and image a lockstep pair.
findings.answer: Required, contract 29→30, with the version.go entry, package.json, version.json, pi-legion AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md in the same change; every fixture and TS literal site listed (T1–T3); the lockstep named in Integration and T7.

findings.finding: Strict object vs open record decides whether every future legion.yaml key becomes a contract bump.
findings.answer: z.looseObject with the two spec-named keys typed (max_fix_attempts, worker_boot_timeout_seconds); the version.go entry says a later legion.yaml key bumps nothing. Precedent: legion-api.ts:178-181's opaque payload.

findings.finding: 'as its legion.yaml sets them' has two readings; the literal-keys reading is not implementable (readKeys discards fileConfig; boot fills resources and plugins) and fails the spec's own example on a file omitting max_fix_attempts.
findings.answer: Resolved values the daemon runs on, in the field's doc comment and the plan; TestSettingsOfAMinimalConfigurationResolvesTheDefaults (omit → 3, set 5 → 5). plugins emitted as settled; PluginsFromBinary excluded as derived.

findings.finding: Leaving runtime.kubernetes.pod out is a departure from 'the rest of that daemon's non-secret settings', and the stated reason (operator free text) applies to omp_launch_prefix, which stays in.
findings.answer: Recorded as spec departure 1 with the distinction: omp_launch_prefix is argv the daemon itself runs and may not run secrets (config.go:85-87); pod is forwarded unread (pod.yml:1-3, kubernetes.go:165-171) and readable from any pod's own spec. The architect decides in or out.

findings.finding: The field widens an unauthenticated read (server.go:179, :233) and the spec never names its audience; app ids, installation ids, image digest, scheduling, agent_secrets url may be called sensitive.
findings.answer: The audience is written into the design (every Legion pod and whatever reaches the port; the spec's shared-ServiceAccount model). Those values stay in as non-secret settings; the ruling is listed for the architect. Duplicates (project, admission_cap, capabilities.decided) are emitted with the trust rule stated.

findings.finding: 'Proven from the controller pod by a negative control' cannot be a curl: the controller runs no bash (SKILL.md:26-31) and nobody may exec into its pod; its only read is op read_state.
findings.answer: T6/T7: envoy_publish to notifications.role.legion-legion-controller asking for a read_state before merge (no settings key) and after deploy (the values); plus the implementer's own curl of $LEGION_DAEMON_URL as a second negative control. Recorded in the PR body's E2E negative control and the handoff proof; the second project's controller read as a comment on LEGION-791, as the spec says.

findings.finding: 'Both daemons run it' and the second project's controller's read depend on a deployment-repository roll these workers never make, on a daemon↔image lockstep, and the dispatch-deploy route fires because packages/contracts/ is in release-envoy-listener.yaml's paths (:17).
findings.answer: T7: both routes per the deployment instructions; the legion-deploy holder pins both daemons; the lockstep named; the dispatch deploy is a no-op rebuild by path rule. No answer from the second project's controller → reported to the architect and republished next wake; the issue waits by default, the architect may accept the LEGION read plus the second project's body.

findings.finding: The controller skill's read_state field list (SKILL.md:26-28) names no settings, and the skill ships inside the plugin.
findings.answer: T5 edits the skill (settings in the list, one sentence on when to read it); scope confirmation requested from the architect.

findings.finding: Stale docs: running-legion.md:515-521's --json list, pi-legion/AGENTS.md's contract prose, CHANGELOG.md; the plain legion state view.
findings.answer: T5 lists each edit; the plain legion state view is unchanged so running-legion.md:508-514's sample stays true (decision 8).

findings.finding: The projection golden (internal/projection/state_golden_test.go:91-94) completes the state by hand and would carry a zero settings otherwise.
findings.answer: T2 completes state.Settings there with api.SettingsOf(config.Config{…}); both -update commands named; one shared fixture config for the api tests and the api golden.

findings.finding: Acceptance lines 2 and 3 had no commands; the second project's daemon is reachable to no LEGION pod.
findings.answer: The acceptance table gives each line a command and expected output; the second project's half is the controller's read_state comment (T7 step 2).

findings.finding: Unverified claims: the controller reads read_state on every wake; the cluster NetworkPolicy's ingress; whether LEGION-781 is live at this merge.
findings.answer: The plan asserts none of them; LEGION-781's timing changes nothing here because the controllers' reads are over Envoy and the record (PR, comment, dispatch comment) is the same with or without a pod.

specDepartures.spec: Done when, line 3: from a Legion pod GET /legion/v1/state names max_fix_attempts, worker_boot_timeout_seconds 'and the rest of that daemon's non-secret settings as its legion.yaml sets them'.
specDepartures.plan: settings carries every key of the resolved legion.yaml except credentials (postgres_dsn, github_apps.*.private_key), their sources (private_key_command, private_key_secret, provider_keys' store key names, session_dsn_secret), the paths of credential files (*_file keys, kubeconfig+context) and the runtime.kubernetes.pod block; provider_keys is the list of variable names.
specDepartures.evidence: deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/pod.yml:1-3 ('Legion knows none of it; it delivers these pieces to every worker pod'); kubernetes.go:165-171 (passed through as written; Kubernetes API types with no legion.yaml-shaped JSON); the spec's 'Kubernetes, allowed' (every pod reads its own spec); config.go:85-87 (omp_launch_prefix may not run secrets, so it stays in). Credential file paths: an unauthenticated route (server.go:179) has no place for a credential's whereabouts.

acceptance: 'and the rest of that daemon's non-secret settings as its legion.yaml sets them' reads as: every key of the resolved file except credentials, their sources, their files, and the operator's pod block (runtime.kubernetes.pod); provider_keys as variable names only.
